item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is the preferable merge candidate because it implements the replayable convenience upload with the established multipart helper while preserving the existing Add and retry machinery. Both candidates incorrectly duplicate Add instead of routing through it, but A additionally makes a broad, contract-prohibited change to RawClient behavior.","reasons":["B keeps the change focused on FilesService.Upload and reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile, whose bytes.Reader result is replayable by net/http.","A changes RawClient.Do to buffer essentially every non-native io.Reader whenever retries are not disabled, altering Add, Update, and unrelated SDK requests despite the contract requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged and forbidding retry-machinery refactoring.","A's global buffering introduces potentially surprising memory use and changes when source-reader errors occur across the SDK, well beyond the few-megabyte Upload convenience API authorized by the contract.","B preserves the exact requested Upload signature, multipart field name \"file\", uploaded filename, response/error shape, and existing FilesOption query/header handling."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's request construction and decoding instead of calling Add, violating the explicit single-path requirement.","The RawClient change broadens behavior globally and can buffer arbitrarily large streaming bodies in memory.","The changelog claims Add and Update now retry and recommends WithNoRetry for streaming, documenting an API behavior expansion specifically outside the frozen scope."],"risks_b":["Upload also duplicates Add's request and response logic rather than simply calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), creating maintenance drift.","Tests omit explicit validation and source-reader-error cases required by the contract.","The retry test counts attempts but does not read and compare multipart content on both attempts, so it does not directly prove that streamed content is resent intact; it also does not visibly set RetryAllMethods: true."]}
